name: Toy.KernelTrust.accepted_semValid_of_faithful_of_semSound
tier_justification: Re-derivation, for a toy logic, of the two-step soundness architecture of verified proof checkers (the implementation accepts only what the inference system derives; the inference system is sound for a semantics), which is mechanised at production scale (Kumar et al. 2016; Candle 2022; Milawa 2015). Tier criterion used throughout: T0 when the statement itself is a published or mechanised theorem; T1 when it is a known observation not previously mechanised in this form.
plain_claim: In the toy rules-as-data propositional logic, if a checker accepts only sequents derivable from the rule table R (`Faithful C R`) and every sequent derivable from R is truth-table valid (`SemSound R`), then every sequent the checker accepts, on any proof object, is truth-table valid; in particular it never accepts `[] ⊢ ⊥`.

hypotheses.name: hFaithful : Faithful C R
hypotheses.purpose: Connects what the implementation accepts to what the rules derive.

hypotheses.name: hSemSound : SemSound R
hypotheses.purpose: Connects what the rules derive to the reference semantics. For the `⊥` part alone, the strictly weaker `Consistent R` suffices (`not_acceptsBot_of_faithful_of_consistent`; strictness: `ex_consistent_not_semSound_anyImpRules`).

depth_justification: The main statement is the composition of the two definitions (a one-line term). It is recorded as an architectural reference point; the work lies in establishing the hypotheses for a given checker and rule table (`recheckRecompute_faithful`, `traceChecker_faithful`, `stdRules_semSound`; card S-recompute, S-semSound).
nonvacuity_witness: The recomputing certificate re-checker for the standard rules is faithful and complete, the standard rules are semantically sound, and the checker accepts a certificate for `[] ⊢ ⊥ → ⊥`.
non_claims: Toy propositional logic only: no binders, dependent types, definitional equality, universes or inductive types. Nothing here is a theorem about Lean, Rocq, HOL Light, Metamath or any production checker.
Nothing about compiled binaries, compilers, runtimes, memory safety, serialisation, I/O or hardware faults. A `Checker` is a mathematical function; the model cannot express miscompilation.
`Faithful` is the soundness direction only (accepted implies derivable). It does not say the checker accepts anything; the reject-all checker is faithful to every rule table.

`SemSound` is relative to the reference truth-table semantics `evalForm`, which is itself trusted and unverified. A misconception shared by the rules and the reference semantics is invisible to every result here.
Says nothing about which statement was checked: a name may resolve to an unintended formula (K2c, K1-pinned).
No completeness claim: `stdRules` is intuitionistic natural deduction and does not derive every truth-table-valid sequent.

design_question: Which assurance layers must a proof-checking pipeline have (implementation faithfulness, semantic soundness of the rules, statement pinning, recomputation of derived certificate data), and which class of defect does each one fail to cover?
grounding_notes: Derived (modeling bridge): Lean4Lean, MetaRocq (MetaCoq), Candle and Milawa are efforts to establish the faithfulness layer for real checkers. The MetaCoq POPL 2020 paper describes its checker as 'proven correct in Coq with respect to its formal specification and axiomatisation of part of its metatheory' and states that 'because of Gödel's incompleteness theorem, there is no hope to prove completely the correctness of the specification of Coq inside Coq ... but it is possible to prove the correctness of the implementation assuming the correctness of the specification, thus moving from a trusted code base (TCB) to a trusted theory base (TTB) paradigm'. That is the faithfulness layer, relative to axiomatised metatheory; it is not a semantic-soundness theorem for the rules.

Derived (modeling bridge): relativised semantic soundness (the `SemSound` layer, established in a stronger metatheory) is what Harrison 2006 (HOL in HOL with an additional axiom), Kumar et al. 2016 and Barras 2010 (set-theoretic models, formalised in Coq, of type theories of the Calculus-of-Constructions family, relative to an axiomatised set theory) establish.

Derived (modeling bridge): the de Bruijn criterion (Barendregt, Wiedijk 2005) asks for proof objects checked by a small independent checker; K1 says what such a checker must additionally satisfy (faithfulness, and sound rules) for its acceptances to be valid.

name: Toy.KernelTrust.pinned_accepted_name_semValid_of_faithful_of_semSound
tier_justification: Comparing the checked statement with an independently held statement is an established practice (Pollack 1998; Adams 2016; the separate specification file of Metamath Zero, Carneiro 2020); not found mechanised in this form.
plain_claim: If a checker is faithful to semantically sound rules, and the statement table P shipped with a proof is pinned to the official table on a name (`Pinned official P name`: the name is defined in the official table and P resolves it to the same formula), then whenever the checker accepts a proof object for that name resolved through P (an empty-context sequent), the official meaning of the name is truth-table valid. The conclusion is stated universally (`∀ φ, official.lookup name = some φ → SemValid [] φ`); it is not vacuous because `Pinned` includes the clause that `name` is officially defined, and under `Pinned` it is equivalent to the existential form 'the name has an official meaning and that meaning is valid' (`pinned_official_meaning_forall_iff_exists`). Without the definedness clause the universal conclusion would hold vacuously for an officially undefined name: it needs only that P agrees with the official table on officially defined names (`accepted_name_semValid_of_faithful_of_semSound_of_agreement`).

hypotheses.name: hFaithful : Faithful C R
hypotheses.purpose: Connects acceptance to derivability.

hypotheses.name: hSemSound : SemSound R
hypotheses.purpose: Connects derivability to validity.

hypotheses.name: hPinned : Pinned official P name
hypotheses.purpose: Connects the formula that was checked (resolved through P) to the official formula. It already asserts that `name` has an official meaning; existence is assumed, not deduced from acceptance. Its definedness clause is not used for the universal conclusion (`accepted_name_semValid_of_faithful_of_semSound_of_agreement`); it is what makes that conclusion equivalent to the existential reading (`pinned_official_meaning_forall_iff_exists`), and `decide (Pinned official P name)` also rejects officially undefined names (`ex_pinned_undefined_neg`).

nonvacuity_witness: The recomputing re-checker for the standard rules, the official table pinned to itself on the name "True", and the certificate topCert, which the checker accepts for that name.
non_claims: The conclusion `∀ φ, official.lookup name = some φ → SemValid [] φ` is trivially true for a name that the official table does not define; the theorem yields 'the official meaning exists and is valid' only through the definedness clause of `Pinned` (`pinned_official_meaning_forall_iff_exists`). A pipeline that compares tables only on officially defined names, without checking definedness, obtains the universal statement and nothing more (`accepted_name_semValid_of_faithful_of_semSound_of_agreement`).

Pinning a theorem's top-level name in a flat lookup table does not prevent soundness or meaning-drift attacks via modified definitional dependencies, hidden axioms in the ambient environment, or duplicate-key shadowing (`StmtTable` uses first-binding-wins `List.lookup`).
`Checker.acceptsNamed` checks empty-context sequents (`[] ⊢ φ`) only; nothing is stated about named statements proved under non-empty assumption contexts or custom axioms.

Toy propositional logic only: no binders, dependent types, definitional equality, universes or inductive types. Nothing here is a theorem about Lean, Rocq, HOL Light, Metamath or any production checker.
The model has no notation, elaboration, parsing or pretty-printing; Pollack-inconsistency (parser/printer round trips, Wiedijk 2012) is not modelled.
A wrong official table is invisible: pinning moves trust to the official table, it does not remove it.

name: Toy.KernelTrust.unfaithful_checker_for_sound_rules_accepts_bot
tier_justification: Folklore (sound rules do not protect against an implementation bug; agreement of checkers is not evidence by itself), made precise as kernel-checked counterexamples.
plain_claim: For the semantically sound standard rules, the re-checker with its hypothesis-membership guard deleted accepts `[] ⊢ ⊥` (only `Faithful` fails). Two quorum variants: a separate-artifact quorum of two differently broken re-checkers accepts `[] ⊢ ⊥` when each member gets its own certificate; and the same-artifact quorum of two different re-checkers that share the missing-guard defect accepts one certificate for `[] ⊢ ⊥`.
nonvacuity_witness: Not applicable: the statements exhibit their witnesses.
non_claims: Toy propositional logic only: no binders, dependent types, definitional equality, universes or inductive types. Nothing here is a theorem about Lean, Rocq, HOL Light, Metamath or any production checker.

`quorum C D` accepts a pair of independent proof objects `(w₁, w₂)`, one per checker; in `separate_artifact_quorum_of_two_unfaithful_checkers_accepts_bot`, the two checkers are given different certificates (`lyingCert .bot` and `bogusHypCert .bot`), each of which the other checker rejects. No single `Cert` is accepted for `[] ⊢ ⊥` by both `recheckTrust stdRules` and `recheckNoHypGuard stdRules` (this follows from `sharedQuorum_recheckTrust_recheckNoHypGuard_faithful`). That theorem therefore does not model two independent checkers accepting the same bogus proof due to a shared defect, nor does it show that disjoint bugs defeat same-artifact N-version checking. The same-artifact cases are `shared_artifact_quorum_of_checkers_with_a_shared_defect_accepts_bot` and `shared_artifact_quorum_of_checkers_with_disjoint_defects_is_faithful`.

Does not say N-version checking is useless: a shared-artifact quorum of two checkers with disjoint defects is faithful here (card S-shared-quorum). Nothing is said about how likely independent implementations are to share a defect.
No claim that any real checker is unfaithful.

Not logically independent of K2b: the trusting re-checker is an unfaithful checker; the content is the mechanism and the paired positive statement.

One derived field in one toy format. The recomputing re-checker ignores the stored field (recompute-and-ignore); it does not validate the field against the recomputed value or report dishonesty (validate-and-reject).

name: Toy.KernelTrust.sharedQuorum_recheckTrust_recheckNoHypGuard_faithful
tier_justification: Folklore (diverse checkers re-checking the same artifact catch defects they do not share), made precise for one pair of defects.
plain_claim: With the translation of proof objects `tr = id` (both members read the identical certificate), for every rule table R the same-artifact quorum of the arity-trusting re-checker and the missing-guard mutant of the recomputing re-checker is faithful to R, although for the standard rules neither member is faithful and their separate-artifact quorum accepts `[] ⊢ ⊥`; under the translator `exploitTranslator`, which shows each member a certificate that exploits its own defect, the same quorum for the standard rules accepts `[] ⊢ ⊥` and is not faithful to them (`shared_artifact_quorum_of_disjoint_defects_accepts_bot_under_exploit_translator`).
depth_justification: Two routine inductions over the certificate list: a certificate accepted by the trusting re-checker passes every hypothesis guard, and on such certificates the mutant runs exactly like the recomputing re-checker.
nonvacuity_witness: For the standard rules: both members are unfaithful, their separate-artifact quorum accepts `[] ⊢ ⊥`, and their shared-artifact quorum accepts the honest certificate for `[] ⊢ ⊥ → ⊥`.
non_claims: Toy propositional logic only: no binders, dependent types, definitional equality, universes or inductive types. Nothing here is a theorem about Lean, Rocq, HOL Light, Metamath or any production checker.
One pair of defects in one format. It does not show that a shared-artifact quorum catches every pair of disjoint defects; here it works because each member enforces exactly the check the other omits.
Says nothing about how likely real independent implementations are to have disjoint defects (K2b's shared-defect example shows they need not).

Same-artifact checking also trusts the translation of proof objects between the two checkers (and any translator or exporter shared by both). `sharedQuorum C D tr` is faithful whenever either member is faithful, for every `tr` (`sharedQuorum_faithful_left`, `sharedQuorum_faithful_right`), but the disjoint-defect result `sharedQuorum_recheckTrust_recheckNoHypGuard_faithful` is stated for `tr = id` only. An untrusted translator that shows each member the artifact exploiting its own defect makes the same quorum accept `[] ⊢ ⊥` (`shared_artifact_quorum_of_disjoint_defects_accepts_bot_under_exploit_translator`). A defective translator, exporter or serialiser upstream of both checkers is therefore not covered by this card.

tier_justification: Trust propagation from a trusted base along verified links is folklore (compare the tower of checkers in Milawa); the ring form with the faithfulness-implies-meta-soundness assumption named was not found in the literature. No novelty is claimed.
plain_claim: In a ring of n verifier nodes sharing one rule table R in which every node accepts a faithfulness certificate for its successor (`RingClosed`), assuming that every node whose object-level checker is faithful also has sound certificate checking (`FaithfulImpliesMetaSound`), if at least one node's certificate checking is sound for claims about ring members (`MetaSound` anchor) then every node's object-level checker is faithful to R; if moreover R is consistent, no node accepts `[] ⊢ ⊥`.

hypotheses.purpose: Propagation passes only through certified links.

hypotheses.name: hFaithfulImpliesMetaSound : FaithfulImpliesMetaSound V R
hypotheses.purpose: Carries the substance: converts faithfulness of a node's object-level checker into soundness of its certificate checking. Not derivable from the `VerifierRing` structure. In a self-hosted ring it follows from claim reflection (`faithfulImpliesMetaSound_of_selfHosted_of_claimReflection`). For n = 1 it is not needed.

hypotheses.name: hAnchor : ∃ i₀, MetaSound V R i₀
hypotheses.purpose: A ring has no base case of its own. For n = 0 it is unsatisfiable.

hypotheses.name: hConsistent : Consistent R (the `⊥` corollary only)
hypotheses.purpose: Turns faithfulness into rejection of `[] ⊢ ⊥`; strictly weaker than `SemSound R`. The counterexample states `¬ SemSound badRules`; that `Consistent badRules` itself fails follows from its `Faithful` and `AcceptsBot` conjuncts (an accepted proof object for `[] ⊢ ⊥` is, by faithfulness, a derivation of `[] ⊢ ⊥`) and is stated directly by `ex_semSound_badRules_neg : ¬ SemSound badRules ∧ ¬ Consistent badRules`.

depth_justification: Induction around the ring. The substance is in the named assumption. Conversely, for n ≥ 1 the conclusion implies `FaithfulImpliesMetaSound` and every anchor (`ring_metaSound_of_all_faithful`), so under `RingClosed` the two assumptions together are exactly as strong as the conclusion: the theorem transports faithfulness, it does not create it.
nonvacuity_witness: `faithfulRing stdRules` (three faithful checkers of different designs: the recomputing certificate re-checker, the trace checker, their separate-artifact quorum) is closed, satisfies `FaithfulImpliesMetaSound`, has a meta-sound node, and the rules are semantically sound and consistent. Its certificate checkers accept every claim; they are meta-sound because every member is faithful.
non_claims: Not 'rings are useless'; this is what a ring buys under the named assumption.
Not 'rings are sufficient': the conclusion is faithfulness only and says nothing about the rules (K3c).

`MetaSound V R i` quantifies only over the fixed nodes `j : Fin n` of the ring `V`, not over arbitrary candidate checkers. Whenever every node of `V` is already faithful to `R` (as in `k3a_nonvacuous` and K3c), `MetaSound` and `FaithfulImpliesMetaSound` hold vacuously even for a rubber-stamp certificate checker or a self-hosted inconsistent rule table such as `badRules` (`ring_metaSound_of_all_faithful`); K3c therefore does not show that an inconsistent logic can serve as a non-trivially meta-sound self-hosted verifier.

`VerifierRing` fixes a single shared rule table `R` for every node in the ring. K3a models multiple checkers implementing the same specification `R`, not a heterogeneous ring of proof assistants implementing distinct logics (such as Lean, Rocq, and HOL Light certifying each other's faithfulness to separate specifications).

Closing a cycle adds no assurance over a directed chain when a known anchor is already faithful and meta-sound; the cycle is used only because the anchor is existential (unknown index `i₀`) and assumed `MetaSound` rather than already `Faithful`. (In `ring_with_uncertified_link_does_not_propagate`, with node 1 as the anchor, the missing link is exactly the one back into the anchor, and the anchor's own object-level checker is the unfaithful one.)
The anchor must be meta-sound for a reason external to the ring; the theorem does not provide one, and without one a closed ring establishes nothing (K3b).

The discriminating power of `MetaSound` (rejecting a false claim) cannot be exhibited inside any ring that satisfies all of K3a's hypotheses with n ≥ 1, since by K3a every member is then faithful; it is exhibited on rings with an unfaithful member (`ex_metaSound_pos`: node 0 of `rubberStampRing`).
Toy model; the toy logic cannot state 'checker j is faithful', so claims are opaque encodings.
Nothing about compiled binaries, compilers, runtimes, memory safety, serialisation, I/O or hardware faults. A `Checker` is a mathematical function; the model cannot express miscompilation.

name: Toy.KernelTrust.consistencyRing_all_inconsistent_of_impClosed_godelIIAnchor_crossHBL
tier_justification: Gödel II and Löb are T0. The two-theory case is folklore, written out informally by Mummert (2013); the n-cycle is the same argument iterated (irreflexivity plus transitivity of 'proves the consistency statement of', compare Mathematics Stack Exchange question 2208419). Polymodal provability logics for several theories (Carlson 1986; Smoryński 1985; Beklemishev 1996; Japaridze, de Jongh 1998) are the classical setting for such arguments; whether the two-theory case is literally a theorem of a specific bimodal logic in those works was not checked against their axiomatisations here, so no such claim is made. Mechanised abstract accounts of Gödel II exist (Popescu, Traytel 2019/2021; Paulson 2015; Saitou, Noguchi 2026 in Lean 4); none of them was found to state the ring form with separately named cross-theory conditions. No novelty is claimed.
plain_claim: For n abstract theories with per-theory provability boxes over one shared sentence language: if every theory is implicationally closed (modus ponens, axiom schemes K and S), at least one theory has Gödel's second incompleteness property in Löb form (`GodelII`: proving its own consistency statement makes it prove ⊥), and the family satisfies the cross-theory Hilbert–Bernays–Löb conditions (`CrossHBL`: cross-necessitation, cross-distribution, formalised Σ₁-completeness for provability statements), then whenever each theory proves the consistency statement of its ring successor, every theory proves ⊥.

hypotheses.name: hImpClosed : ∀ i, ImpClosed i
hypotheses.purpose: Each theory chains implications. Modus ponens is used at every theory, K and S only at the anchor. Ex falso is not assumed.

hypotheses.name: hGodelII : ∃ i₀, GodelII i₀
hypotheses.purpose: Carries the substance of Gödel's second incompleteness theorem, assumed at one node only. For concrete theories it follows from Löb's theorem (`LobRule.godelII`), i.e. from D1–D3 plus the diagonal lemma; the interface has no diagonal lemma, so it is assumed. Unsatisfiable for n = 0.

hypotheses.name: hBridge.nec : ∀ i j, CrossNec i j
hypotheses.purpose: Theory i verifies actual proofs of theory j. Used at the anchor and on the ring links `CrossNec i (ringNext i)`.

hypotheses.name: hBridge.distrib : ∀ i j, CrossDistrib i j
hypotheses.purpose: Theory i proves theory j closed under modus ponens (cross-theory normality). Used at the anchor only.

hypotheses.name: hBridge.sigma1 : ∀ i j k, CrossSigma1 i j k
hypotheses.purpose: Theory i proves that theory j verifies proofs of theory k (formalised Σ₁-completeness for provability statements). Used at the anchor only.

hypotheses.name: hRing : ∀ i, Thm i (con (ringNext i))
hypotheses.purpose: The cycle itself.

depth_justification: Derived from K4a-local (the anchor proves ⊥) plus backward propagation along the ring (`inconsistent_of_proves_con_of_inconsistent`). The diagonal of `CrossHBL` (each theory's own D1–D3) is not used; the substance of Gödel's theorem is inside the assumed `GodelII`.
nonvacuity_witness: All hypotheses hold together in `trivialFamily (Fin n)` for every n ≥ 1 (necessarily an inconsistent family, by the theorem). Each tightness witness is a family in which every other hypothesis holds and every theory is consistent.
non_claims: About abstract `ProvFamily` structures only. The result applies to a concrete formal system only insofar as that system, with a concrete choice of provability predicates and a common sentence language, satisfies every named condition; this package verifies the conditions for no concrete theory.

Dropping Löb's rule or Gödel's second incompleteness property (or `CrossSigma1`, `CrossNec`, `CrossDistrib`) at a single node or in a single direction does not escape K4a: as soon as even one node `i₀` satisfies the Gödel-II instance (`Thm i₀ (con i₀) → Thm i₀ bot`), implicational closure, and the cross-theory conditions from `i₀` to the other theories, `i₀` proves `⊥` (K4a-local), and `CrossNec` on the ring links together with the ring hypothesis and modus ponens forces every other node to prove `⊥` as well. For every theory of the ring to be consistent, every theory must fail at least one of its own anchor conditions (`ImpClosed`, `GodelII`, `CrossHBLFrom`); breaking a single ring link `CrossNec i (ringNext i)` only shields theory `i` from inheriting an anchor's inconsistency (`one_unverified_ring_link_leaves_anchor_inconsistent`). In K4b's two-theory countermodel `starFamily 2`, both `CrossSigma1 0 1 0` and `CrossSigma1 1 0 1` fail.

K4a excludes cycles of categorical consistency proofs (`Thm i (con (ringNext i))`); it does not exclude mutual relative consistency proofs or equiconsistency (`Thm i (con i → con j)` and `Thm j (con j → con i)`), nor mutual interpretability between consistent theories of equal consistency strength (such as ZF and ZFC, or PA and ACA₀).

`ProvFamily` assumes all `n` theories share a single sentence type `Sent` with common `bot`, `imp`, and provability boxes. Applying K4a to distinct concrete formal systems (such as Lean and Rocq) additionally requires translating provability statements into a common syntactic fragment (such as arithmetic) so that the bridge conditions hold across those translations.

Like K4b's `starFamily`, the abstract models `leafFamily` and `possibilityFamily`, and theory 1 of `oneBrokenNecFamily`, contain consistent theories that prove their own inconsistency statement `□ᵢ⊥` (and in `leafFamily` and `possibilityFamily` every theory proves every `□ⱼ□ₖ⊥`, so `CrossSigma1` holds there vacuously): `finite_countermodels_prove_own_inconsistency`. They establish logical independence of K4a's conditions, not the existence of Σ₁-sound theories exhibiting those behaviours. The positive control `omegaChainFamily` and the K4b variant `omegaStarFamily` contain no theory proving its own inconsistency statement.
Does not say one theory cannot prove another's consistency (`consistency_proof_along_open_chain_is_consistent`).

Does not exclude infinite descending sequences of theories each proving the next one's consistency (Pakhomov, Walsh 2021, abstract: 'it is possible to construct descending chains of artificial theories with respect to consistency strength').
`GodelII` is a hypothesis; the package proves Gödel's second theorem or Löb's theorem for no theory.

Not a statement about proof checkers or kernels: reading it as 'two type theories cannot prove each other consistent' requires verifying every named condition, and a common sentence language, for those theories.
About consistency statements `□ⱼ⊥ → ⊥` only; it does not address relativised soundness results (soundness assuming a stronger principle), which is how real self-hosted soundness proofs are stated.

name: Toy.KernelTrust.two_consistent_theories_prove_each_others_consistency_without_crossSigma1
tier_justification: A routine polymodal Kripke countermodel; polymodal provability logics and their Kripke semantics are classical (Carlson 1986; Beklemishev 1996; Smoryński 1985). No source stating this countermodel was found; no novelty is claimed.
plain_claim: Dropping only formalised Σ₁-completeness (`CrossSigma1`), two (indeed any n ≥ 2) consistent abstract theories exist that prove each other's (their successor's) consistency statement while satisfying every other hypothesis of K4a and K4a-local, with `CrossSigma1` failing in both directions; a variant exists in which no theory proves its own inconsistency statement.

hypotheses.name: hn : 2 ≤ n (`consistencyRing_consistent_without_crossSigma1` and `consistencyRing_consistent_without_crossSigma1_not_proving_own_inconsistency` only; `two_consistent_theories_prove_each_others_consistency_without_crossSigma1` is closed and `starFamily_proves_own_inconsistency` has no hypothesis)
hypotheses.purpose: A ring of consistency proofs between distinct theories needs at least two theories. For n = 1 the ring successor of theory 0 is theory 0 itself (`ringNext 0 = 0`), and neither `starFamily 1` nor `omegaStarFamily 1` proves its own consistency statement, so the ring conjunct fails; for n = 0 there is no theory, so the conjunct `¬ ∀ i, Thm i ⊥` fails.

nonvacuity_witness: Not applicable: the statements exhibit their witnesses (the hypothesis `hn : 2 ≤ n` of the two general-n statements holds, for example, for n = 2).
non_claims: Does not exhibit real formal systems that consistently prove each other's consistency; the theories are artefacts of Kripke models and their boxes are not arithmetised provability predicates.

In `starFamily` each theory, although consistent, proves its own inconsistency statement `□ᵢ⊥` (`starFamily_proves_own_inconsistency`); `omegaStarFamily` removes that defect, and no theory of `omegaStarFamily n` proves any `□ⱼ□ₖ⊥` (`omegaStarFamily_not_proves_nested_box_bot`), so it has neither of the finite-model artefacts listed under K4a's non-claims.

Standard provability predicates in theories strong enough to formalize Σ₁-completeness (such as extensions of `IΣ₁`) satisfy `CrossSigma1`, whereas sufficiently weak theories (such as Robinson's `Q`) or non-standard provability predicates can fail it; K4b's abstract Kripke model shows logical necessity of `CrossSigma1` in `ProvFamily`, not how concrete theories fail it.
Breaking `CrossSigma1` in one direction only would not suffice (K4a-local): both `CrossSigma1 0 1 0` and `CrossSigma1 1 0 1` fail in `starFamily 2`.
Shows necessity of one condition at a time.

name: Toy.KernelTrust.inconsistent_proves_every_local_reflection_of_mp_efq
tier_justification: Ex falso inside the theory; the local reflection schema is classical (Kreisel, Lévy 1968).
plain_claim: An abstract theory that is closed under modus ponens, has ex falso, and proves ⊥ proves the local reflection schema `□ⱼA → A` and the consistency statement of every theory in its family, itself included; so an unconditional self-soundness theorem is not evidence of soundness.

hypotheses.name: hMp : MpClosed i
hypotheses.purpose: Combines the ex falso instance with ⊥. Counterexamples: `local_reflection_fails_without_mp` (reflection form) and `con_fails_without_mp` (consistency form).

hypotheses.name: hEfq : HasEfq i
hypotheses.purpose: Supplies `⊥ → (□ⱼA → A)`. Essential for the reflection form (`local_reflection_fails_without_efq`, whose theory has the axiom schemes K and S). For the consistency form it can be replaced by the axiom scheme K (that ex-falso-free witness still proves every consistency statement); `con_fails_without_efq` is a theory with neither ex falso nor K that is closed under modus ponens, proves `⊥`, and proves no consistency statement.

hypotheses.name: hInconsistent : Thm i bot
hypotheses.purpose: The theory is inconsistent.

depth_justification: One application of modus ponens to an ex falso instance.
non_claims: About abstract `ProvFamily` structures only. The result applies to a concrete formal system only insofar as that system, with a concrete choice of provability predicates and a common sentence language, satisfies every named condition; this package verifies the conditions for no concrete theory.

The implication from inconsistency (`Thm i bot`) to every local reflection schema (`□ⱼA → A`) depends essentially on ex falso quodlibet (`HasEfq`) and does not apply to paraconsistent or minimal-logic theories (`local_reflection_fails_without_efq`); deriving `con j := □ⱼ⊥ → ⊥` from `Thm i bot` requires only modus ponens and either ex falso or the axiom scheme K.

Proving implementation faithfulness (that a checker accepts only derivations of a specification `R`) inside a system implementing `R` is not a proof of the local reflection schema `□A → A` or of `Con(R)`, and is not forbidden by K5 or Löb's rule.
K5 alone does not say that a system proving its own soundness is inconsistent; that needs Gödel's second incompleteness property (K5-iff).

The schema is local reflection `□A → A` over the abstract sentence language; nothing is said about uniform reflection, typed soundness theorems, or soundness proofs carried out in a stronger metatheory.
Not 'verified or self-verified kernels are worthless': relativised results are untouched.
